whatItDoes: Turn one blog post or transcript into a tweet thread, LinkedIn post, newsletter, quote graphics, and a short clip, then fan the pack out by email to everyone on your list. Runs on a schedule against your latest post, or with `dryRun` to read the copy before anything is generated.
longDescription:
Give it one blog post or transcript and it hands you a whole content pack: a tweet thread, a LinkedIn post, a newsletter section, quote graphics, and a short teaser clip. An LLM (`models.run`) rewrites the source into every channel at once, keeping your meaning instead of inventing new claims.

From there it makes the media, one async job at a time: a quote graphic per pull-quote (`images.launch`), then the first graphic animated into a short clip (`video.launch`). Each job runs in the background and the agent run pauses until a webhook says it's ready, costing nothing while it waits.

It gathers everything into one markdown pack, saves a durable copy to file storage, then fans the pack out — one email per recipient on your `deliverTo` list. A bad or placeholder address degrades that one recipient rather than sinking the run; the result names exactly how many of your recipients it delivered to.

It ships with a `schedule` input, so you can point it at your latest post and let it run on a cron cadence instead of by hand. Set `dryRun` and it stops right after writing the copy, returning the text without paying for any images or video.

You pay for one LLM call, one image per quote, one short clip, and one email per recipient — the waiting is free. Start with a small `numQuotes`; the images and the clip are the pricey part.
notes:
Click **Use this template** — Sapiom builds and deploys it for you; open it on the **Agents** page and run it. Your $5 signup credit covers first runs.

`source` is the only required input — paste the blog post or transcript text. Set `dryRun: true` to stop after writing the copy and read it without paying for any images or video. A full run bills the LLM, one image per quote, one short image-to-video clip, and one email per recipient, so keep `numQuotes` small (default 2, max 4). To have it email the pack, set `deliverTo` to one or more addresses — the pack fans out, one send per recipient; without it the run returns the pack and says nothing was sent. Give it a `schedule` (a cron string) to run it as a standing job.

Prefer to work from the code? Run it locally with `run_local` and `{ "dryRun": true }` to trace the copy step for free, or edit and deploy it with the Sapiom MCP.
